patient.chief_complaint: Found unresponsive in bed by family, brief shaking witnessed earlier, persistent confusion now 55 minutes
patient.hpi: A 77-year-old White female retired librarian was brought to the emergency department by her son after she was found increasingly difficult to rouse this morning. Her son reports she lives alone and had called him last night complaining of a headache and feeling 'fuzzy-headed.' When he arrived this morning, she was in bed, and he witnessed what he described as generalized stiffening and rhythmic jerking of her arms and legs lasting approximately 2 minutes. After the shaking stopped, she was still not back to normal. He called 911. On EMS assessment, 30 minutes after the observed seizure, she was awake but staring blankly, answering only 'yes' or 'no,' with significant word-finding difficulty. She has a history of hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and moderate Alzheimer's dementia. She lives alone with daily check-ins from her son. Her baseline per son is that she is oriented to her name and sometimes the year, speaks in short sentences, needs help with medications, but is independent with basic ADLs. She takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation, donepezil, and lisinopril. Her son reports her INR was therapeutic at her last check 3 weeks ago (2.4). However, she has been taking several doses of over-the-counter ibuprofen for back pain for the past 10 days. She has no prior history of seizures. No recent falls per son. Temperature at scene 38.0°C per EMS. Urine was foul-smelling per son who changed her pad this morning. Son suspects urinary tract infection.

ct.impression: NEUROSURGICAL EMERGENCY. Acute-on-chronic right frontoparietal subdural hematoma (SDH) 12 mm with 8 mm midline shift and early right uncal herniation. Anticoagulation (warfarin) with critical INR 4.8 — immediate reversal with 4-factor PCC and vitamin K required. Emergent neurosurgery consultation for SDH evacuation. NCSE likely secondary to SDH mass effect on right temporal cortex.
recommended_actions: IMMEDIATE 4-factor PCC (Kcentra) for rapid INR reversal in life-threatening hemorrhage
IV vitamin K 10 mg slow infusion
Emergent neurosurgery consultation for SDH evacuation
Monitor for herniation — emergent neurosurgery needed

interactions.description: Ibuprofen (and all NSAIDs) markedly potentiate warfarin's anticoagulant effect via two mechanisms: (1) displacement of warfarin from plasma protein binding sites, raising free warfarin concentration; (2) inhibition of COX-1 platelet function, additive bleeding risk with anticoagulation. 10 days of ibuprofen 1200 mg/day has caused INR to rise from therapeutic 2.4 to critical 4.8. Combined bleeding risk: extreme.
interactions.clinical_recommendation: Stop ibuprofen immediately. Reverse warfarin with 4-factor PCC (Kcentra) + IV vitamin K 10 mg. Warfarin should be held until INR corrects to <1.5 for surgical intervention. After healing, consider aspirin-free pain management or acetaminophen for future analgesic needs.

output.summary: NSAID + warfarin = major interaction causing critical INR 4.8 and hemorrhagic SDH. Immediate PCC reversal required. INR 4.8 at risk for further bleeding expansion. Stop NSAID. Never co-prescribe NSAIDs with warfarin without close INR monitoring.

output.impression: NCSE resolved post-SDH evacuation and AED treatment. Residual LPDs expected from traumatic cortical irritation. Continue levetiracetam. Clinical correlation recommended.

Post-SDH evacuation changes. No new acute infarct. Alzheimer's dementia changes with small vessel disease. Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) pattern on SWI — increased future ICH risk; anticoagulation decision requires careful risk-benefit analysis with neurology and cardiology. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: warfarin restart after subdural hematoma atrial fibrillation cerebral amyloid angiopathy risk

results.title: Restarting anticoagulation after subdural hematoma: systematic review
results.key_finding: Risk-benefit for anticoagulation restart after SDH: CHADS2-VASc score vs HAS-BLED score must be balanced. CAA pattern on MRI significantly increases hemorrhagic recurrence risk. Consider alternative direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban) which have lower intracranial hemorrhage risk than warfarin. Restart generally after 4-8 weeks for low-moderate bleeding risk; individual decision for high-risk (CAA, elderly).

output.summary: After SDH in elderly patient with CAA, warfarin restart is controversial. If AF stroke risk high (CHA2DS2-VASc), consider switch to apixaban (lower intracranial hemorrhage risk vs warfarin). Avoid NSAIDs permanently — never prescribe concurrently with anticoagulants without close INR monitoring.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Acute-on-chronic subdural hematoma causing NCSE, precipitated by warfarin supratherapeutic INR (4.8) from ibuprofen-warfarin interaction in elderly woman with Alzheimer's dementia; UTI and hyponatremia as secondary precipitants

Sodium 130 contributes to lowered seizure threshold but is not the primary cause; SDH + NCSE explain the clinical picture; hyponatremia is secondary from ibuprofen water retention + UTI SIADH

critical_actions: Stat CT head BEFORE any other intervention in anticoagulated patient with new focal signs — exclude SDH/hemorrhage
4-factor PCC + vitamin K for CRITICAL INR 4.8 with active hemorrhage — emergent reversal
Stop ibuprofen immediately — major warfarin interaction causing life-threatening SDH
Emergent neurosurgery for SDH evacuation with early herniation
Do NOT perform LP before CT when focal signs present and anticoagulation supratherapeutic
Levetiracetam dose reduction for AKI — 750 mg BID not 1000 mg BID
contraindicated_actions: LP before CT and INR correction — catastrophic herniation risk in anticoagulated patient with SDH and midline shift
Continuing ibuprofen or NSAIDs with warfarin — caused the hemorrhagic complication
Administering tPA — SDH and hemorrhagic emergency, no ischemic stroke
Standard levetiracetam dose (1000 mg BID) without renal adjustment — AKI Cr 1.4 requires dose reduction
Using warfarin long-term without consideration of CAA — cerebral amyloid angiopathy on MRI warrants apixaban or anticoagulation risk-benefit reassessment
key_reasoning_points: NSAIDs + warfarin = major interaction via protein-binding displacement + platelet inhibition — INR can surge dramatically; ibuprofen caused SDH by raising INR from 2.4 to 4.8
In any anticoagulated patient with new focal signs + seizure, CT head FIRST to exclude hemorrhage before LP or anticoagulant continuation
4-factor PCC (Kcentra) corrects INR within 15-30 minutes — vitamin K alone takes 6-12 hours (too slow for emergent SDH)
UTI + hyponatremia are secondary precipitants that lower seizure threshold in demented elderly — but the structural lesion (SDH) is the primary driver of NCSE
Levetiracetam dose must be renally adjusted in AKI — Cr 1.4 in 77yo female = GFR ~35-40 mL/min; 750 mg BID maximum
CAA pattern on MRI: anticoagulation restart after SDH requires careful risk-benefit analysis; apixaban has lower ICH risk than warfarin in AF
